flora: 36 woody species in 16 families recorded in 10 plots (Fabaceae richest, 7 spp.); timber species logged include Iroko (Milicia excelsa), Obeche (Triplochiton scleroxylon), mahogany, Opepe (Nauclea diderrichii), African copaiba balsam (Daniellia oliveri), Gmelina; shea (Vitellaria paradoxa) and Prosopis africana cut for firewood/charcoal
threats: Farming, logging, fuelwood, grazing. Farming/cropland expansion, illegal logging, grazing and herder settlements inside the reserve, fire, firewood and charcoal, settlement and construction; deforestation escalated after 2000
notes: Gazetted 1966 (as Doma Native Area FR); lost ~83% of forest 1966-2020, cropland ~65% of reserve by 2020. One of Nasarawa State's 41 gazetted reserves charted in 1966. Landsat analysis 1986-2020 found Doma lost 83% of its forest cover, with cropland covering 65% of the reserve; NDVI fell sharply between 1999 and 2015.

name: Sambisa Forest Reserve
vegetation: Sudan-Guinea savanna: mostly Sudan-zone thorn-tree savanna with Northern Guinea broad-leaved savanna in the south; open woodland and dense thorny bush, becoming more Sahelian where disturbed
flora: Acacia senegal, Acacia polyacantha, Combretum glutinosum, Adansonia digitata, Tamarindus indica, Anogeissus leiocarpus, Balanites aegyptiaca, Prosopis africana, Detarium macrocarpum, Vitex doniana, Diospyros mespiliformis, Piliostigma thonningii, Dalbergia melanoxylon, Commiphora africana
fauna: Historically: African elephant, leopard, lion, hyena, baboon, roan antelope, red-fronted gazelle, oribi, waterbuck, warthog, hartebeest; 62 bird species incl. bateleur, secretarybird, Arabian bustard. Thought to be Nigeria's last ostrich site
tourism: Safari tourism with lodges and cabins operated from the 1970s. These were destroyed after insurgents took over the forest in 2013, and the area is currently inaccessible.
threats: Armed conflict and military bombardment; fuelwood felling and charcoal burning; farm clearing and settlement; livestock grazing; poaching including elephants; over-fishing with chemicals
notes: The reserve was gazetted in 1958 and re-gazetted as a National Game Reserve in 1977. Boko Haram has used it as a base since 2013, and ISWAP has controlled it since May 2021. A July 2006 aerial count found no live elephants, only a few antelopes, and about 21,400 cattle with 203 settlements. Sources differ on the area: the game reserve is often given as 518 km², the KBA as 688.71 km², and the atlas polygon as 165 km².

name: Kogin Kano Forest Reserve
vegetation: Open Northern Guinea savanna woodland with Sudan savanna elements in the north; trees 9-14 m; drained by the Kano River and its tributaries (Maiwa, Kumbo, Randa); Lake Tiga forms the northern boundary.
flora: Isoberlinia doka, Khaya senegalensis, Vitex doniana, Anogeissus leiocarpus, Tamarindus indica, Detarium microcarpum, Pterocarpus erinaceus
fauna: Roan antelope (Hippotragus equinus), hartebeest (Alcelaphus buselaphus), buffalo (Syncerus caffer), red-flanked duiker, red-fronted gazelle (VU), lion (VU) - populations very low, some possibly locally extinct; birds include white stork, red-footed falcon, bateleur, Abyssinian ground hornbill; 261 species recorded
resources: Protects the Tiga Dam catchment (reduces siltation for the Kano River Project); microclimate and windbreak benefits for nearby villages.
tourism: River Kano rapids and rock formations, the old ghost town of Falgore with traditional architecture, nearby camping; the river is navigable from Tiga Lake in the wet season.
threats: Poaching, illegal grazing, overfishing (including chemical poisons), bush fires, farming encroachment, kidnapping/insecurity.
notes: Began as Kogin Kano Forest Reserve in the colonial 1940s and was upgraded to a game reserve and renamed Falgore Game Reserve in the 1960s; part of the Falgore and Lame Burra Game Reserves Key Biodiversity Area (IBA), with a recommendation to merge both and upgrade to national park. Area figures vary (KBA ~92,000 ha; Wikipedia ~1,000 km2).

name: Kanawa Forest Reserve
vegetation: Sudan savanna woodland. Mosaic of dense Sudan savanna on hills with riparian, marshy and lowland forest along the Poli stream, tall-grass grassland, and thorn forest in drier parts; altitude 336-390 m
flora: Azadirachta indica (dominant), Azanza garckeana, Raphia sudanica, Elaeis guineensis, Senna siamea, Ficus congoensis, Ficus polita, Gmelina arborea, Azadirachta indica, Anogeissus leiocarpus, Vitex doniana, Albizia lebbeck
resources: Fuelwood, grazing. Former tree nursery supplying roadside and town planting across Gombe division
threats: Fuelwood cutting, encroachment.

name: Lame Forest Reserve

fauna: Birds of the combined Falgore-Lame Burra KBA include white stork, red-footed falcon, Abyssinian ground hornbill; lion and red-fronted gazelle reported at very low numbers, possibly extirpated
threats: Poaching, illegal grazing, over-fishing (including chemical poisons), bush fires, tree felling and farmland allocation (Ningi side), insecurity: in 2020 legislators reported bandits and other criminal groups based in the reserve
notes: Facts here refer to Lame Burra Game Reserve (reported at 205,900 ha, gazetted 1972), where 101 plant species have been recorded. This reserve appears to be its Lame section: the match is based on name and location (Toro LGA) and no source confirms it. In January 2022 Bauchi State revoked illegal land allocations in the reserve and banned farming there. The West African Conservation Network is working with the state government on management, ranger capacity and habitat restoration.

name: Falgore (Kogin Kano) National Park
authority: National Park Service; Kano State Government (KAZOWMA)
vegetation: Northern Guinea savanna woodland, Sudan savanna in north.
flora: Savanna woodland (Isoberlinia, Afzelia, Daniellia types), Adansonia digitata, Tamarindus indica, Faidherbia albida, Vitex doniana, Pterocarpus erinaceus, Vitellaria paradoxa
fauna: Roan, hartebeest, buffalo, red-flanked duiker, red-fronted gazelle, lion (likely extirpated), 261 bird spp. incl. white stork, ground hornbill, Roan antelope, lion (very low/locally lost), 261 bird spp. incl. Abyssinian ground hornbill, bateleur
resources: Watershed for Lake Tiga and Kano River, grazing, Watershed of Tiga Dam (Kano River Project), fisheries, fuelwood
tourism: Rock formations and rapids of the Kano River, Falgore ghost town; river navigable from Tiga Lake in wet season; camping near reserve. Game viewing and birding ~110 km south of Kano along the Kano–Jos road; Lake Tiga forms northern boundary.
threats: Poaching, illegal grazing, chemical fishing, bush fires, farming encroachment, kidnapping/insecurity.
notes: Former Kogin Kano Forest Reserve (1940s), upgraded to game reserve; WDPA also lists the overlapping Kogin Kano FR polygon (~757 km²). Proposed for national park status. Listed as 'Galgore NP' in the 2023 approval; Kogin Kano FR (1940s) then game reserve (1960s). Area ~1,000 km² (approx).

governance: Federal or national ministry or agency
designations: IBA; KBA; UNESCO MAB (Oban); UNESCO MAB (Okwangwo)
vegetation: Lowland and submontane rainforest, montane grassland on ridges. Lowland Guineo-Congolian rainforest (Pleistocene refuge).
flora: ~1, 568 plant spp. (77 endemic to Nigeria): African mahogany, red ironwood (Lophira alata), African corkwood, epiphytic ferns and orchids, 545 spp. in 98 families incl. Ancistrocladus korupensis, Prunus africana, ebony
fauna: Forest elephant, chimpanzee, drill, Sclater's guenon, 75+ mammals, 350+ birds (incl. olive ibis), 42 snakes, ~950 butterflies, Cross River gorilla, Nigeria-Cameroon chimpanzee, Preuss's guenon, grey-necked rockfowl, golden greenbul, grey parrot
resources: Timber, bushmeat, NTFPs (bush mango, Afang/Gnetum), watershed, NTFPs, medicinal plants
tourism: Kanyang tourist village ~1 h from Calabar, Kwa Falls, Agbokim Falls, forest hiking and birding; contiguous with Korup NP (Cameroon). Gorilla tracking, hiking near the Obudu Plateau; borders Takamanda NP (Cameroon).
threats: Illegal logging, slash-and-burn farming, hunting, chemical fishing, plantations at margins. Logging, snaring/poaching, farming, cattle grazing.
notes: Formed from Boshi, Okwangwo and Boshi Extension Forest Reserves; Cross River gorilla stronghold. Southern and larger division of CRNP, carved from Oban Group Forest Reserve.
other_names: Cross River National Park – Okwangwo Division.

name: Yankari Game Reserve
vegetation: Sudan-Guinea savanna with riparian forest along Gaji river.
flora: Savanna woodland, riparian forest, wild baobab, Borassus palms, Isoberlinia doka, Daniellia oliveri, Anogeissus leiocarpa, Vitellaria paradoxa
fauna: Savanna elephant, lion (near extinct), hippo, buffalo, roan, waterbuck, baboons, 350+ birds (saddle-billed stork), African bush elephant, lion, roan antelope, hartebeest, baboon, 350+ bird spp
resources: Warm springs, NTFPs, Water (Gaji, Yashi, Yuli streams), wildlife
tourism: Nigeria's best-known wildlife destination: Wikki Warm Springs, game drives, Marshall Caves, Dukke iron-smelting furnaces.
threats: Poaching, grazing incursions; lion near extinction. Poaching (elephant), grazing, decline of lions.
notes: Constituted as Bauchi NA forest reserve 1957, opened as game reserve 1962; national park 1991-2006, then returned to state as game reserve.
other_names: Yankari Game Reserve (former Yankari National Park).

name: Old Oyo National Park
governance: Federal or national ministry or agency
vegetation: Guinea savanna woodland with gallery forest and inselbergs.
flora: Savanna woodland trees (Isoberlinia, Daniellia, Vitellaria), riparian forest
fauna: Buffalo, kob, roan, western hartebeest, waterbuck, bushbuck, patas monkey, birds
resources: Water (River Ogun, Ikere Gorge Dam), grazing, minerals
tourism: Ruins of Oyo-Ile (old Oyo Empire capital), Ikere Gorge Dam, caves, rock shelters, inselberg climbing.
threats: Poaching, logging, herder encroachment, illegal mining.
notes: Formed from Upper Ogun (1936) and Oyo-Ile (1941) Forest Reserves.

name: Gashaka-Gumti National Park
governance: Federal or national ministry or agency
vegetation: Guinea savanna (Gumti) to montane forest and grassland (Gashaka).
flora: Afzelia africana, Khaya senegalensis, Daniellia oliveri, Isoberlinia doka, Vitellaria paradoxa, Triplochiton scleroxylon, Pterocarpus erinaceus
fauna: Largest chimpanzee population in Nigeria, buffalo, elephant, giant eland, roan, leopard, lion (rare), wild dog, 500+ birds
tourism: Chappal Waddi (2,419 m, Nigeria's highest peak), Kiri waterfall, hippo pool, hot spring, German fort ruins on Gashaka Hill.
threats: Rosewood logging, grazing, poaching, insecurity.
notes: Nigeria's largest national park; home to Gashaka Primate Project.

name: Kamuku National Park
governance: Federal or national ministry or agency
vegetation: Sudan-Guinea savanna woodland with riparian forest.
flora: Isoberlinia doka, Afzelia africana, Daniellia oliveri, Detarium, Terminalia avicennioides, Raphia, Andropogon gayanus
fauna: Elephant, roan, western hartebeest, oribi, red-flanked duiker, patas monkey, baboon, 177 birds (secretarybird, ground hornbill, Denham's bustard)
tourism: Elephants, Dogon Ruwa waterfalls, Goron Dutse inselberg, Tsaunin Rema boulder hill, birding.
threats: Banditry (operations suspended 2021), hunting, cattle grazing.
notes: Gazetted 1936 as Birnin Gwari Native Authority Forest Reserve; upgraded 1999.

name: Yankari Forest Reserve
vegetation: West African savanna; bush savanna on sandy soils east of the Gaji valley
fauna: African bush elephant, olive baboon, patas monkey, roan antelope, lion, African buffalo, waterbuck, bushbuck, hippopotamus; 350+ bird species incl. saddle-billed stork, helmeted guineafowl, African grey hornbill
tourism: Yankari is Nigeria's best-known wildlife destination, with several natural warm-water springs, and was opened to the public on 1 December 1962. Archaeological sites, including old iron-smelting furnaces and caves at Delimiri and Ampara, support heritage tourism.
threats: Lion population reported to be close to local extinction; illegal activities
notes: The game preservation area was approved in 1956, constituted as a Bauchi Native Authority Forest Reserve in 1957 and declared a national park by Decree 36 of 1991. National park status was withdrawn in 2006 at the Bauchi State Government's request. Wikipedia gives the area as about 2,244 km², compared with the atlas polygon's 2,134 km².

name: Baturiya Wetland
vegetation: Intermittent floodplain lakes and Acacia–doum palm woodland.
flora: Acacia nilotica, Mitragyna inermis, doum palm, Borassus, baobab, wild rice
fauna: Pelicans, yellow-billed stork, knob-billed duck, garganey, crocodiles, monitor lizards
tourism: Birdwatching; part of Hadejia Wetlands NP.
threats: Upstream dams, siltation, invasive grasses, illegal grazing.
notes: Ramsar no. 1752; part of Hadejia-Nguru wetlands.

name: Dagona Sanctuary Lake Ramsar Site
governance: Federal or national ministry or agency
designations: Chad Basin NP; IBA (Hadejia-Nguru wetlands); Ramsar; Waterfowl Sanctuary
vegetation: Seasonally flooded oxbow lake in Hadejia-Jama'are floodplain. Seasonal oxbow lake with Mitragyna and doum palm woodland.
flora: Mitragyna inermis, doum palm, Borassus, Acacia, Parkia, Khaya senegalensis
fauna: 20, 000+ waterbirds: herons incl. goliath, egrets, pelicans, spur-winged goose, spoonbill, red-fronted gazelle, 25+ waterbird spp, wintering Palaearctic ducks, breeding grey heron, little egret, fishes
tourism: Dagona Waterfowl Sanctuary: birdwatching base for the Hadejia-Nguru wetlands. Bird hides, platforms and nature trails in the Dagona Waterfowl Sanctuary.
threats: Grazing and wild-resource collection despite prohibitions. Grazing, fuelwood, upstream dams, drought.
notes: Dagona Waterfowl Sanctuary, Ramsar No. 1753; managed within the Bade-Nguru sector of Chad Basin NP.

name: Upper Orashi Forests Ramsar Site
flora: Lophira alata, Hallea ledermannii (abura), Sacoglottis, Ricinodendron, Irvingia, Raphia hookeri, rattan, Ricinodendron heudelotii, Albizia adianthifolia, Hallea ledermannii, oil palm
fauna: Sclater's and white-throated guenons, Delta red colobus, pygmy hippo, black-fronted duiker, grey parrot roost, Sclater's guenon, white-throated guenon, red colobus
tourism: Limited; research/education potential. Ecotourism limited by insecurity.
threats: Uncontrolled logging, oil access roads, farm clearing, insecurity. Poaching, uncontrolled logging, militancy.
notes: Ramsar site since 30 Apr 2008 (25,165 ha); forest reserve ~10,384 ha (FAO). Ramsar no. 1759; gazetted FR 9,696 ha within site.

name: Foge Islands Ramsar Site
vegetation: Seasonally flooded grassland islands in Kainji Lake.
flora: Nymphaea lotus, Echinochloa, Vossia cuspidata, Cyperus, Andropogon, Hyparrhenia, Echinochloa pyramidalis, E. stagnina, Cyperus procerus
fauna: 180+ birds (whistling ducks, pratincoles, spur-winged goose, glossy ibis), hippo, kob, waterbuck, hartebeest, 180+ bird spp. (white-faced whistling-duck, collared pratincole, blue-cheeked bee-eater)
resources: Fishing (~5, 000 residents), recession farming, grazing, Fisheries
tourism: Birding by boat on Lake Kainji next to Kainji Lake National Park.
threats: Low lake levels and drought, overfishing, fuelwood cutting, hunting.
notes: Island in Lake Kainji; permanently exposed parts lie in Kebbi State, western section in Niger State. Ramsar no. 1754; in northern Kainji Lake.

name: Lake Chad Wetlands in Nigeria Ramsar Site
vegetation: Lake, floodplain marsh, Typha/papyrus swamps and Sahel shrubland. Grasses, sedges, floating macrophytes, shrubs.
flora: Typha australis, Cyperus papyrus, Mimosa pigra, Acacia nilotica, doum palm, Prosopis juliflora, wild rice
fauna: 300+ birds (ferruginous duck, pallid harrier, great snipe), lungfish, Clarias, tilapia, Kouri cattle, Palaearctic waterbirds incl. marbled teal, indigenous fishes
resources: Fishing, rice and recession farming, grazing, Fisheries, recession farming
tourism: Limited by insecurity.
threats: Lake recession, dams, desertification, overgrazing, Boko Haram insecurity. Lake recession from drought and upstream dams; insecurity.
notes: Ramsar No. 1749; only traditional (Kanuri) management of fishing and farming rights. Largest Nigerian Ramsar site; unprotected.

name: Apoi Creek Forests Ramsar Site
vegetation: Tidal freshwater swamp forest, mangrove, marsh.
flora: ~240 spp.: Rhizophora, Uapaca paludosa, Nauclea, Raphia, Irvingia, Hallea ledermannii, Pterocarpus soyauxii
fauna: Niger Delta red colobus, dwarf crocodile, sitatunga, leopard, grey parrot, Hartlaub's duck, African skimmer, Niger Delta red colobus (endemic, CR), fish spawning grounds
resources: Fishing, logging, salt, NTFPs, canoe carving, Fish, timber
tourism: Community conservation areas around Apoi, Kokologbene and Gbanraun. Creek and boat tourism potential.
threats: Logging canals, oil spills and flaring, hunting. Timber extraction via dug canals, hunting.
notes: Ramsar site (30 Apr 2008); includes Apoi Creek FR (7,080 ha, FAO). Ramsar no. 1751; now within Apoi National Park.

name: Lower Kaduna–Middle Niger Floodplain
vegetation: Floodplain marsh, Mitragyna swamp forest, Guinea savanna.
flora: Nymphaea lotus, Echinochloa, Vossia, Phragmites karka, Mitragyna, Mimosa pigra
fauna: Rosy bee-eater and carmine bee-eater colonies, Hartlaub's duck, woolly-necked stork, grey pratincole, Gymnarchus, Lates, Heterotis fish
resources: Fishing, fadama rice/sugarcane farming, grazing, fuelwood
tourism: Bee-eater colonies and river birding.
threats: Upstream dams (Kainji, Jebba, Shiroro), intensive fadama farming, overfishing.
notes: Ramsar no. 1755; otherwise unprotected.

name: Oguta Lake
governance: Federal or national ministry or agency
vegetation: Natural freshwater lake with swamp and relict forest.
flora: Nymphaea lotus, Pistia, Vossia, Lophira alata, Pycnanthus, Ricinodendron, oil palm
fauna: ~40 fish spp. (Chrysichthys, Lates, Tilapia), Sclater's guenon in relict forests
resources: Fishing, transport, sand dredging, water supply
tourism: Lakeside hotel and golf course, boat rides; Imo's largest natural lake.
threats: Overfishing, dredging, sewage, algal blooms, gully erosion.
notes: Ramsar no. 1757.

name: Pandam and Wase Lakes
vegetation: Savanna lakes with gallery forest and woodland.
flora: Afzelia africana, Ceiba pentandra, Raphia sudanica, Isoberlinia doka, Parkia biglobosa, Vitellaria paradoxa
fauna: West African manatee, hippo, Nile crocodile, roan, buffalo, 217 birds (Pel's fishing owl, long-toed lapwing)
tourism: Annual fishing festival, birdwatching, Pandam tourist village (20 chalets).
threats: Poaching, overfishing, grazing/burning, farm conversion.
notes: Ramsar no. 1758.

name: Chad Basin National Park – Chingurmi-Duguma Sector
vegetation: Sudan–Guinea savanna to Sahel; Acacia–Balanites woodland
flora: Acacia spp., Balanites aegyptiaca, elephant grass, wild sorghum
fauna: Savanna elephant (~100 in 2007), black crowned crane, demoiselle crane, white stork, helmeted guineafowl
tourism: Game viewing and birding near the Cameroon border; lodges abandoned, off-road access and camping needed.
threats: Poaching, farming/grazing encroachment, Boko Haram insecurity
notes: Largest of Chad Basin NP's three separate sectors; transboundary elephant range with Waza (Cameroon).

name: Chad Basin National Park – Bade-Nguru Wetlands Sector
vegetation: Seasonal floodplain wetlands, doum palm and Acacia woodland; includes 5 forest reserves
flora: Hyphaene thebaica, Acacia spp., Mitragyna inermis, wild rice
fauna: Palearctic migratory waterfowl (garganey, ruff), herons, pelicans, red-fronted gazelle
tourism: Includes the Dagona Waterfowl Sanctuary with bird hides and trails; prime winter birdwatching.
threats: Reduced flooding from upstream dams, quelea poisoning, cultivation, tree loss
notes: Part of the Hadejia-Nguru wetlands complex.

name: Chad Basin National Park – Bulatura Oases Sector
vegetation: Swampy inter-dune valleys (oases) between Sahelian sand dunes
flora: Doum palm, Acacia, Sahelian grasses
fauna: Sahelian birds and small mammals (poorly documented)
tourism: Scenic dune and oasis landscapes near the Niger border.
threats: Desertification, grazing
notes: Smallest sector of Chad Basin NP.

name: Apoi National Park
flora: Rhizophora mangroves, Raphia, Irvingia, Uapaca, Nauclea, Hallea ledermannii, Xylopia staudtii
fauna: Niger Delta red colobus, Sclater's guenon (?), dwarf and Nile crocodile, sitatunga, leopard, grey parrot, Hartlaub's duck
tourism: Riverine boat-based ecotourism potential.
threats: Logging canals, oil spills, gas flaring, hunting, land-tenure disputes
notes: Former Apoi Creek Forest Reserve (Ramsar 2008); upgraded to national park (NASS approval 2023). Area is Ramsar boundary.

name: Hadejia Wetlands National Park
vegetation: Seasonal floodplain wetlands with Acacia–doum palm woodland
flora: Acacia nilotica, Mitragyna inermis, Hyphaene thebaica, Borassus, Anogeissus leiocarpus, baobab, wild rice
fauna: Pelicans, yellow-billed stork, knob-billed duck, white-faced whistling duck, garganey (20,000+ waterbirds), crocodiles
tourism: Waterbird watching in the dry season; state tourism development planned.
threats: Upstream dams (Tiga, Challawa), siltation, invasive Typha, illegal grazing/fuelwood
notes: Former Baturiya Wetland Game Reserve; FG took over 10 Sep 2024. Area is Ramsar boundary.

name: Kampe National Park
authority: National Park Service (handover from Kwara State, 2025).
tourism: Planned ecotourism; named after the Kampe River.
notes: WDPA lists Ebbe/Kampe at 117.3 km2; approved in 2020 for upgrade to national park and handed to the Federal Government in Feb 2025 (overlaps national-park layer). Coordinates are GeoNames River Kampe FR. Former Kampe (Ebbe/Kampe) forest and game reserve; handed to NPS Feb 2025. LGA as reported by ThisDay; coordinates approx.

name: Marhai National Park
vegetation: Guinea savanna with gallery forest on escarpment. Guinea savanna and hills.
fauna: Diverse wildlife (undocumented), Monkeys, guinea fowl
tourism: Contains Farin Ruwa waterfall (~150 m), picnic site, Kulere culture. Scenic landscape; ecotourism, research and education planned. Promoted by the state for eco-tourism, research and education for its scenic landscape and wildlife.
notes: Gazetted 1960 by Northern Region; upgraded to national park (FG takeover Dec 2024) - overlaps national-park layer. Former Marhai (Marhi) Forest Reserve; upgrade process began 2011; FG takeover Dec 2024. In Wamba LGA; the upgrade effort began in 2011 and in December 2024 the Federal Government took over management for the National Park Service as a national park.

name: Pandam National Park
authority: Plateau State Government (approved 2020 for NP upgrade). National Park Service.
vegetation: Sudan-Guinea savanna with gallery forest; Pandam Lake (~2 km²).
flora: Afzelia africana, Ceiba pentandra, Raphia sudanica, Burkea africana, Isoberlinia doka
fauna: West African manatee, hippo, roan, buffalo, duikers, warthog, 217 birds (Pel's/Bouvier's fishing owl, long-toed lapwing), hippopotamus, roan antelope, buffalo (formerly), olive baboon, white-faced whistling duck, Pel's fishing owl
tourism: Game viewing, birding, sport fishing, canoeing on Pandam Lake; 20 chalets (dilapidated). Pandam Lake boating, sport fishing, bird watching, chalets (some derelict).
threats: Poaching, grazing, bush burning, logging, illegal fishing, encroachment. Poaching, grazing, bush burning, neglect, floodplain rice schemes.
notes: Game reserve since 1972; one of 10 reserves approved in 2020 for upgrade to national park - may overlap national-park layer. Pandam Wildlife Park/Game Reserve (1972); upgraded to national park (NASS approval 2023). KBA gives 33,048 ha.

name: Nguru Lake (and Marma Channel) Complex
vegetation: Floodplain lakes, channels and marshes with doum palm uplands. Sahelian floodplain lake, marsh and fadama.
flora: Echinochloa, Nymphaea, Typha, Ceratophyllum, doum palm, tamarind, wild rice
fauna: Garganey (20, 000+ wintering), ruff, white-faced whistling duck, ~65 fish spp, white-faced whistling duck (each >20, 000), disc tilapia
resources: Fisheries, recession farming, grazing, fuelwood, groundwater recharge, flood-recession farming
tourism: Boat rides and birdwatching; IUCN wetland information centre. Boat-based ecotourism at Dabar Magini; winter birdwatching.
threats: Typha invasion, upstream dams, grazing, cultivation, overfishing. Invasive Typha, upstream dams, overgrazing, fuelwood harvest.
notes: Ramsar site designated 2 Oct 2000, core of the Hadejia-Nguru wetlands. RIS coordinates are garbled; placed at Nguru town. Nigeria's first Ramsar site (21 Mar 2000), Ramsar no. 1039.

name: Maladumba Lake
vegetation: Shallow Sudan-savanna lake with surrounding forest reserve. Permanent lake and marsh within savanna forest reserve.
flora: Acacia nilotica, Tamarindus indica, baobab, Typha, Mimosa pigra (~175 spp.)
fauna: ~82 birds (ruff, grey heron), buffalo, bushbuck, patas monkey, Lates, Bagrus, Hydrocynus, white-necked stork, green fruit pigeon, diverse fishes
resources: Fishing, irrigation, grazing, fuelwood, Fisheries, farmland
tourism: Birdwatching and lakeside recreation potential. Annual fishing festival.
threats: Rapid siltation, fires, unregulated fishing/hunting. Rapid siltation, farming, grazing, hunting.
notes: Ramsar site (No. 1756) comprising the lake and its surrounding forest reserve. Ramsar lists 10.4N 9.85E; GeoNames places the lake in Misau LGA. Ramsar no. 1756; surrounded by Maladumba Forest Reserve (51.8 km²).

name: Ado-Awaye (Iyake) Suspended Lake Wetland
vegetation: Hilltop (suspended) lake on inselberg with woodland
flora: Afzelia africana (VU), Albizia zygia, Antiaris toxicaria, Parkia biglobosa, Ficus
fauna: Mona monkey, bushbuck, Nile crocodile, Nile monitor, egrets, woolly-necked stork
tourism: Hike to Africa's rare suspended lake atop Oke-Ado; sacred Ishage rock.
threats: Farming, tree felling, unregulated tourism/religious use
notes: Ramsar no. 2550 (1 Mar 2024).

name: International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA) Ramsar Site
vegetation: Reservoir lake and regenerated lowland rainforest (protected since 1965)
flora: Ceiba, Milicia, Terminalia, bamboo, Raphia, oil palm
fauna: 300+ birds incl. Ibadan malimbe (EN), great snipe; mona monkey
tourism: Birdwatching, forest walks and canoeing at IITA campus, Ibadan.
threats: Urbanisation, siltation, invasive species
notes: Ramsar no. 2551 (1 Mar 2024); inside 1,000 ha IITA campus.

name: Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove
designations: UNESCO World Heritage; UNESCO World Heritage Site
vegetation: Riverine primary high forest along Osun River.
flora: 400+ spp.: Terminalia ivorensis, Ceiba, Triplochiton, Milicia excelsa, Brachystegia nigerica, 400+ plant species, 200+ medicinal
fauna: White-throated guenon (EN), red-capped mangabey (EN), mona monkey, pangolin, pythons, catfish
resources: Sacred forest, medicinal plants, Sacred/cultural forest
tourism: UNESCO World Heritage site with ~40 shrines and sculptures; annual Osun-Osogbo Festival (August).
threats: Historical hunting, fishing, felling, land speculation. Urbanisation, invasive plants, tourism pressure.
notes: Sacred grove; 47 ha buffer zone. Ramsar no. 2563 (1 Mar 2024).

name: Ebute Oni Coastal Wetland
vegetation: Coastal lagoon mangrove and swamp forest
flora: Rhizophora racemosa, Nypa palm, Raphia hookeri, Lophira alata, Nauclea diderrichii
fauna: Crocodiles, waterbirds, Sclater's guenon (reported), sea turtles (reported)
resources: Artisanal fishing, rice farming, water transport
tourism: Annual festivals and lagoon recreation.
threats: Water hyacinth, agriculture, effluents, sea-level rise
notes: Ramsar no. 2564 (1 Mar 2024).

name: Arinta Waterfall
flora: Ricinodendron heudelotii, Ceiba pentandra, Milicia excelsa, Alstonia boonei, Pycnanthus angolensis
fauna: Mona monkey, red-capped mangabey, bushbuck, red-flanked duiker, grey parrot, endangered damselflies
tourism: Multi-tiered waterfall at Ipole-Iloro near Ikogosi Warm Springs; swimming and hiking.
threats: Deforestation, unregulated tourism
notes: Ramsar no. 2565 (1 Mar 2024).

name: Yemoji Lake, Ijebu-Ode
tourism: Lake in Ijebu-Ode town with cultural significance.
notes: Listed Nigerian Ramsar site (184.1 ha); details not verified.

name: Ogoni Mangrove Wetland
vegetation: Mangrove forest, tidal creeks, mudflats and islands
flora: Mangroves (Rhizophora, Avicennia), Nypa palm
fauna: Finfish, shellfish, crustaceans, crocodiles, turtles, grey parrot
tourism: Mangrove restoration showcase (HYPREP).
threats: Oil pollution legacy, illegal refining
notes: Designated Mar 2026 after HYPREP clean-up; coordinates at Bori (approx).

name: Omo Biosphere Reserve (incl. Strict Nature Reserve)
authority: Ogun State Forestry Department / UNESCO MAB.
designations: Forest Reserve; IBA; Strict Nature Reserve; UNESCO MAB
vegetation: Mixed moist semi-evergreen lowland rainforest, plantations.
flora: Diospyros spp, Khaya ivorensis, Cordia millenii, Dracaena mannii, Gmelina and teak plantations, Dracaena manni
fauna: Forest elephant, chimpanzee, white-throated monkey, pangolin, yellow-casqued hornbill, rich butterflies, African elephant, civet, long-crested eagle
resources: Timber, fuelwood, farming, NTFPs, fishing in transition zone
tourism: Elephant camp research station; forest birding and butterfly watching. Research and nature tourism around the strict nature reserve core.
threats: Logging, farm encroachment, erosion, biodiversity loss.
notes: UNESCO biosphere (1977): 460 ha core strict nature reserve, 8,165 ha buffer, ~666,499 ha transition; ~6,000 residents. Nigeria's first biosphere reserve (core 460 ha Omo SNR; ~130,500 ha forest reserve).
other_names: Omo Biosphere Reserve / Omo Strict Nature Reserve

name: Oban Biosphere Reserve
flora: 1,568 plant spp.
fauna: Cross River gorilla, Nigeria-Cameroon chimpanzee, forest elephant, drill
tourism: Rainforest ecotourism via Cross River NP (Oban).
threats: Logging, farming, hunting
notes: Core 195,771 ha; includes Oban FR, CRNP and Obudu Plateau.

name: Okwangwo Biosphere Reserve
flora: ~1,545 spp. in 98 families
fauna: Cross River gorilla, chimpanzee, drill, Preuss's guenon, elephant, grey-necked rockfowl
tourism: Gorilla habitat near Obudu Mountain Resort.
threats: Shifting cultivation, hunting
notes: Core 83,060 ha; centred on CRNP Okwangwo division (coords from division).

name: Hadejia-Nguru-Bade Biosphere Reserve
flora: Doum palm, Acacia, Typha, wild rice
fauna: 377 bird spp. incl. ferruginous duck, pallid harrier, great snipe
tourism: Winter waterbird watching (Dagona, Nguru).
threats: Dams, Typha invasion, drought
notes: Designated under BIOPALT (Lake Chad) project.

name: Shere Hills Biosphere Reserve
vegetation: Montane grassland and rocky hills of the Jos Plateau (to 1,759 m)
tourism: Hiking and rock climbing on the Jos Plateau's highest hills, ~10 km east of Jos.
notes: Cited by UNESCO/FRIN as a Nigerian biosphere reserve; designation year not verified.

name: Ohunbe Forest Reserve
notes: Western Ogun (Yewa) reserve per GeoNames; little documented.

name: Oja-Odan Forest Reserve
notes: Listed among Ogun's nine forest reserves; located at Oja-Odan town (approx).

name: Ologe Lagoon Forest Reserve
notes: Lagoon-fringe reserve listed in Beak (1998) inventory.

name: Yelwa Forest Reserve
notes: Small reserve listed under Lagos in Beak (1998); location unverified.

name: Lufasi Nature Park
fauna: Wildlife rescue/rehabilitation sanctuary
tourism: Forest tours, lakes, eco-hall, picnic and play areas on Lekki–Epe Expressway (km 41).
notes: Private NGO-run urban forest park.

name: Okoo Forest Reserve
notes: ~0.7% of Oyo reserve area.

name: Olaseinde Forest Reserve
notes: Small reserve (~0.2% of Oyo reserve area).

name: Ago-Are Forest Reserves I & II
notes: Listed among Oyo's nine reserves.

name: Oke-Iho Forest Reserve
notes: Listed among Oyo's nine reserves.

name: Old Ogbomoso Waterworks Forest Reserve
notes: Watershed protection reserve.

name: Ogunpa Forest Reserve
tourism: Urban forest behind Agodi Gardens, Ibadan.
threats: Felling and proposed conversion to residential/commercial use
notes: Early indigenous-species plantation; watershed of Ogunpa River.

name: IITA Forest Reserve (Ibadan)
fauna: Rich bird community incl. Ibadan malimbe
tourism: Forest school, trails, canopy tower, birdwatching (Ibadan Bird Club).
notes: ~350 ha of forest on IITA's 1,000 ha campus; recognised IBA.

name: Oyinmo Forest Reserve
notes: Listed as 'Oyinno' in GeoNames.

name: Ada Forest Reserves (1 & 2)
notes: Listed under 'Ondo/Ekiti' (668 + 401 ha) in Beak (1998); location unverified.

name: Idanre Hills (Oke Idanre)
fauna: Rock hyrax, monkeys, bat colony
tourism: Hilltop heritage site (Owa's palace, shrines), ~3,000 ft; Ogun and Ije festivals; popular hiking.
threats: Hunting
notes: On UNESCO World Heritage tentative list (2007).

name: Gelegele Forest Reserve
fauna: Forest elephant, white-throated monkey
tourism: Accessed by boat; 30-year conservation/eco-tourism concession to Africa Nature Investors Foundation (2022).
threats: Illegal logging, uncontrolled farming
notes: Second largest reserve in Edo after Okomu; contiguous with Okomu NP landscape.

name: Sokponba Forest Reserve
flora: Opepe, Afara (Terminalia), Mahogany, Albizia, Alstonia, Okwen
threats: Deforestation

name: Lekki Conservation Centre
fauna: Mona monkey, bushbuck, Maxwell's duiker, crocodile, monitor lizard, many birds
tourism: Canopy walkway (among Africa's longest), tree house, nature trail, boardwalks; major Lagos ecotourism site.
threats: Urban development pressure
notes: Urban nature reserve managed by the Nigerian Conservation Foundation.

name: Farin Ruwa Forest Reserve
tourism: Surrounds the Farin Ruwa waterfalls in Wamba LGA, which the state plans to develop for tourism (including a proposed 'Film City').
threats: Encroachment by loggers and herders; grazing and tree cutting are prohibited
notes: News report (Feb 2021) of the state government vowing to protect the reserve and waterfalls.
